title: Document and history
description: The puzzle being edited (one per engine): new, open, import, save, the Puzzlecad export, grid conversion, the notes, undo and redo. A new document drops every playback and explorer handle.

document.new.summary: A new empty puzzle on a grid; the grid never changes. The open document goes (as with document.open, document.openBytes and solve.importPaused): its solves pause and are waited for, its analyses stop, its handles are dropped, and after the reply its problems whose work the events were reporting get a last solve.state idle and solution.analyseEnded (stopped); the revision counts on.

document.open.summary: Opens a .xmpuzzle file (gzip or plain XML; one that inflates to more than 256 MiB is refused as parse_error); what this version does not model is kept. The open document goes as with document.new.

document.openBytes.summary: Opens a puzzle from its file's bytes (gzip or plain XML; gzip that inflates to more than 256 MiB is refused as parse_error), base64; the document has no path unless one is given. The open document goes as with document.new.

path.description: The file these bytes stand for: the document's path, where document.save writes (a rescue copy of a puzzle that has a file).

dirty.description: The document starts with unsaved changes (a rescue copy): dirty until saved.

document.import.summary: Imports another program's puzzle file (File ▸ Import ▸ PuzzleSolver3D or Puzzlecad (OpenSCAD)) as a new, untitled document with unsaved changes: a cube-grid puzzle with one problem, its pieces one of each; Save then asks where to write the ShapeLogic file, never over the source. The file is read by its path or from its bytes, exactly one of the two, as it is (never decompressed), at most 256 MiB; one whose shapes would hold more than 2^27 cells together is refused (parse_error), as is one the format's reader cannot take (the original's "Could not load puzzle, sorry!"). The open document goes as with document.new.

format.description: puzzleSolver3D: a PuzzleSolver3D file (.puz): PIECE and RESULT size lines, each followed by the shape's rows, its layers side by side. puzzlecad: a puzzlecad OpenSCAD file (.scad): the pieces of its burr_plate and burr_piece calls, its first packing_box as the result (else a cube of variable cells).

document.exportPuzzlecad.summary: The puzzlecad OpenSCAD file of a problem's pieces (File ▸ Export ▸ Puzzlecad (OpenSCAD)): the distinct shapes of its parts but the result (when that leaves none, every shape but the result), or every shape when no problem is given, each as the layers of its bounding box in one burr_plate, in the layout of puzzlecad's MagellanTIC.scad. The header comment names the document's file, or `name` when it has none ("unknown" without either). Only for cube-grid puzzles with shapes (the original's "Puzzlecad export is only available for cube-grid puzzles.", "Nothing to export."), and some shape must have a cell ("Could not export puzzlecad file."): invalid_argument. Allowed while solving.

name.description: The file being written, for the header when the document has no file. At most 255 bytes, no control characters.

document.convertGrid.summary: The puzzle on another grid (Edit ▸ Convert brick grid type to other): each cube of a cube-grid puzzle becomes the cells that fill it (5x5x5 on the rhombic grid, 3x3x3 on the tetra-octa grid), the shapes keep their names, the colours and the notes stay, and each problem's definition is copied with its name, without its solutions. As the original, the document is replaced: it has unsaved changes, nothing to undo, and keeps its path, so document.save writes the converted puzzle over the file it came from. The grids a puzzle converts to are engine.info's grids[].convertsTo; another is unsupported. Refused while solving (invalid_state), and when the converted shapes would hold more than 2^27 cells together (invalid_argument). The open document goes as with document.new.

document.save.summary: Saves (gzip, as the original) to the path given, or to the document's path; the document is clean afterwards. Refused while a solve runs: save at a save point (solve.savePoint).

document.saveBytes.summary: The file's bytes (plain XML), base64, without marking the document clean.

document.setNotes.summary: The puzzle's comment. Allowed while solving. Control characters other than tab, newline and carriage return are refused (the file is XML 1.0); a name (shape.rename, problem.rename) refuses line breaks as well, since an attribute would give them back as spaces.

edit.undo.summary: Undoes the last step. Refused while solving or inside edit.begin / edit.end.

edit.history.summary: The labels of the undo and redo steps.

undo.description: Oldest first; the last is undone next.

edit.begin.summary: Groups the following calls into one undo step (a drag across cells); groups do not nest.

edit.end.summary: Ends the group; an empty group leaves no step.

document.changed.summary: The document changed: after a call that changed it, and when a solve run ended or an analysis was applied. Empty id lists mean the lists themselves changed (or anything of that kind).

notice.description: What the change did beyond what was asked, to tell the user: a sliding piece whose new shape lost its starts and goals. Only when there is something to tell.
